title: Your Moat Is Your Data Model — Mike Phipps, Gates Foundation
talk_summary: Mike Phipps describes the Gates Foundation's Strategic Intelligence Platform, a Neo4j knowledge graph that unifies siloed systems of record (funding, management, people, documents) into one semantic layer exposed to agents via MCP. The core claim is that the durable moat is the modeled tacit process knowledge, and that eval-driven gap-finding is how you harden that data model.

takeaways.technique: Unified semantic graph layer behind MCP instead of per-agent ad-hoc retrieval
Eval questions with live-graph ground truth and pass@1 + stability
takeaways.what_they_do: For each eval question they pre-build a graph query, run it against the live graph at eval time as ground truth, compare to the agent's answer with an LLM judge, and track pass@1 plus answer stability across repeated asks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we pull from the live graph and then we compare that to what the agent is delivering for that question

takeaways.technique: Eval failures feed back into schema/domain-rule descriptions
takeaways.what_they_do: When evals fail, they treat it as a data-model or domain-rule gap and update schema descriptions and domain rules, closing the loop rather than tweaking prompts per case.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's a feedback loop here that you you can update then your your data model
we've actually modified these quite a bit here. We forked it

takeaways.technique: Constrained workflow experiences over free chat, same backend
takeaways.what_they_do: Beyond general chat, they expose constrained workflow UIs (MCP apps) that pull from the same graph backend, limiting the agent's action space for specific tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It helps to constrain the experience compared to chat, but it at the same time it pulls from that same knowledge graph-based uh back-end platform
